target_customer: Hardware and mechanical engineering teams at manufacturers, from startups to Fortune 500 firms
problem: Engineering design reviews relied on spreadsheets and email, with feedback scattered and hard to track against 3D CAD files.
product_category: Design review and collaboration software for hardware engineering

founders.name: Jeremy Andrews
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Mechanical engineer from Newfoundland who designed Model 3 battery pack components at Tesla. Education not stated on the page.

founders.name: Adam Keating
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page and CoLab Series B release (CEO and co-founder). Mechanical engineer with work on a hyperloop vehicle and radiotherapy systems per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser based viewing of 3D CAD files with comments and issue tracking needs CAD format handling and rendering, standard but nontrivial engineering for a student founded team.

defensibility.rationale: Review history and CAD integrations create switching costs for engineering teams, while a review viewer alone could be copied by CAD vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CAD vendors offered built in commenting, but CoLab grew independently and raised large rounds in 2024 and 2025 with no acquisition.

market_need_then: The founders saw large hardware companies run design reviews on spreadsheets during their Tesla and RefleXion co-ops, described as archaic in coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses colabsoftware.com, not the exact .com; the name also collides with Google Colab.

identity.voice_and_tone: Engineer to engineer, built by engineers who lived the problem

branding.community_and_virality: Founder story of a second place Paradigm Hyperloop finish at the SpaceX competition and regional press in Newfoundland.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable founder story and regional pride, but the name is generic and sources show little brand-level press.

outcome_analysis: CoLab turned a student hyperloop team experience into a design review platform used by large manufacturers. After a 2018 pre-seed and a 2019 post-YC seed it raised a 21 million dollar Series B in May 2024 led by Insight Partners and a 72 million dollar Series C in November 2025, and launched an AI AutoReview product. It is a strong, growing, active company with 150 staff.
notes: The pre-seed was 600,000 Canadian dollars so amount_usd is null. The 2.7M seed figure comes from an Entrevestor headline and a CBC headline about fall 2019 funding; the currency and exact date were not confirmed, and ZoomInfo lists 2.1M dollars, treated as conflicting. The Series B 21M dollars is stated by the company and several outlets (BetaKit, Pulse 2.0, The Logic). The Series C is stated by the company and multiple outlets, one outlet said 98M, treated as an outlier. The YC page also mentions an October 2021 BetaKit article about 21M in funding, which conflicts with the 2024 date; the dated company release is used. Total raised is not stated by the company. No competitor sourced near May 2019 was found, current review sites list Onshape and Fusion as alternatives but are undated and not used. Founder education not found on opened pages.
